 Print Actor Nitish Bharadwaj , best known for playing Lord Krishna in BR Chopra's 'Mahabharat', has changed his stance on Ranbir Kapoor and Yash's 'Ramayana: Part 1'. Following the film's trailer release, the actor had praised Nitesh Tiwari 's ambitious project and even predicted that it could win an Oscar for Best Foreign Film. However, after watching the film, Bharadwaj has expressed strong disappointment, stating that it does not deserve to represent Indian cinema on the international stage. He believes the film has misrepresented Bharat's story and strayed from the spiritual and civilizational significance of the Ramayan. Taking to Instagram, Nitish Bharadwaj shared a lengthy note explaining his objections to the film. He emphasised that the Ramayan is not merely a story but a mahakavya deeply connected to the cultural, spiritual and civilizational consciousness of Sanatan Bharat. He also pointed out that its central characters, including the heroines and antagonist, are integral to the values and message of the epic. According to him, Mahavishnu took the avatar of Rama to uphold dharma, parampara and establish maryada. Watch Nitish Bharadwaj: Irrfan’s strengths lay in his eyes, diction and sense of timing Criticising the portrayal of Ravana in the film, the actor wrote, "By presenting Ravan as an exceptionally liberal, socially just and fair figure, the film, in my view, alters the moral framework of the Ramayan and undermines the very purpose of avataar," Bharadwaj also revisited his earlier positive reaction to the film's trailer, making it clear that his opinion changed after watching the final product. Expressing his disappointment, he stated, "I cannot find a single good word to say about it. A spectacle of VFX can never substitute for the core values, philosophical depth and spiritual essence of this Mahakavya." He further questioned whether the film should represent Indian cinema internationally, stressing that filmmakers must handle the country's cultural legacy with responsibility. "This film, in my opinion, does not deserve to represent Indian cinema internationally when its narrative misrepresents Bharat's history, heritage and core spiritual values," he added. Directed by Nitesh Tiwari, 'Ramayana: Part 1' arrived in theatres on November 5. Ranbir Kapoor plays Lord Rama, Sai Pallavi essays Goddess Sita, while Yash portrays Ravana. The film also features Ravi Dubey as Lord Lakshman, Arun Govil as King Dashratha, Indira Krishna as Mata Kaushalya and Lara Dutta as Kaikeyi. Sheeba Chadha plays Manthara. Rakul Preet Singh, Vivek Oberoi and Kunal Kapoor are also part of the ensemble cast. Meanwhile, the film has maintained a strong run at the box office, collecting over Rs 350 crore net in India and crossing the Rs 500 crore mark worldwide. With its global earnings continuing to grow, the Ranbir Kapoor and Yash starrer is now eyeing the Rs 700 crore milestone.
